notes:
Colorado imposes no franchise or privilege tax on a default LLC. The evidence is the Department of Revenue's own business-tax index, which enumerates exactly six tax types - Sales & Use Tax, Business Income Tax, Withholding Tax, Excise & Fuel Tax, Severance Tax and Property Taxation (DOLA) - and names no franchise tax; that is the index a franchise tax would appear in. The 2024 C.R.S. Title 39 text corroborates the absence: the only occurrences of "franchise tax" in the whole title are the apportionment provisions describing taxes other states impose, and there is no franchise-tax article. The recurring entity-level levy Colorado does impose is the business income tax, which is a tax on income and therefore outside this namespace's inclusion test.
stateIncomeTax: members owe Colorado income tax on their pass-through shares - the filing-requirements page puts every resident and nonresident with Colorado-source income under the return requirement, and the business income tax page puts the LLC itself under a Colorado income tax return. The rate is a flat 4.4%, printed in the 2025 DR 0104 booklet ("The income tax rate is currently 4.4%").
hasPTETElection is true through the SALT Parity Act (SB 22-124): partnerships and S corporations may elect annually to be subject to Colorado income tax at the entity level. The Department's page names partnerships and S corporations rather than LLCs; a default LLC is a partnership for federal tax purposes, which is how it reaches the election, and the record says so rather than overstating the page.
collectedWithAnnualReport is null by construction: with no franchise-type levy there is no overlap with root states.json's annual_report_fee (25 for Colorado, the SOS annual report filing).
needsReview: Nothing is in doubt. The absence finding could be sharpened from the statute itself - the DOR index says what Colorado levies, and the C.R.S. Title 39 structure corroborates it, but no single statutory sentence states "Colorado imposes no franchise tax on LLCs". A future session could cite a Department publication answering what an LLC owes annually if one is published.
